events.outcome: Current first-party help confirms PAYG-only remains available, web/manual credit starts at $20, SMS top-ups can add $10 with a saved card, standalone PAYG expires 90 days after purchase, and first activation must occur on a U.S. network tower. International roaming also requires prior U.S. line use.

2026 community evidence is mixed for overseas SMS continuity: one Tello tutorial thread reports Codex verification SMS not arriving, while a separate long-running overseas user reports SMS/2FA abruptly stopping after months of Wi-Fi Calling. These reports do not isolate PAYG-only plan state tightly enough for a service aggregate, so preserve them as route-level risk evidence rather than manufacturing an app success rate.

Tello publicly acknowledges automated and human fraud-prevention checks can decline orders; community replies in the same provider-moderated thread describe account suspensions and concern about preserving long-held numbers. This is a continuity risk signal, not a quantified suspension probability.

data.acquisitionSummary: Tello Pay As You Go is a separate credit product from the monthly-plan route. Web PAYG orders start at $20; domestic rates are 1¢/min, 1¢/SMS and 2¢/MB.

keep.action: Place a new PAYG order before 90 days have elapsed since the last PAYG order when no active monthly plan is keeping the credit valid. Usage such as sending an SMS does not reset this order-based expiry.

data.chinaActivation: Initial SIM/eSIM activation or port-in must be completed while physically in the United States and connected to Tello US network towers. After US activation, Wi-Fi Calling & Text or international roaming may be used abroad.
data.kyc: No ID verification; email + payment method only.
data.payment: International cards widely reported accepted; PayPal also accepted.
data.wifiCalling: Supported and documented by Tello; primary route for using US number abroad.
data.roamingSms: Standard international roaming in 200+ countries uses PAYG credit and requires prior use of the line in the United States. Destination-specific China rates are not asserted here without a current direct destination quote.
data.tariffSummary: $20 minimum web PAYG order; credit expires 90 days after the last PAYG order unless an active plan keeps it valid. US rates: 1¢/min, 1¢/SMS, 2¢/MB. Sending an SMS does not reset PAYG expiry.
guideSteps: Order at least $20 of Tello PAYG credit.
Complete first SIM/eSIM activation in the United States on Tello network towers.
If no active monthly plan is preserving the credit, place a new PAYG order before 90 days elapse; ordinary SMS usage does not reset this clock.
After prior US use, enable Wi-Fi Calling & Text or international roaming as needed abroad.

data.acquisitionSummary: Tello Pay As You Go is a separate credit product from the monthly-plan route. Web PAYG orders start at $20; domestic rates are 1¢/min, 1¢/SMS and 2¢/MB.

keep.action: Keep PAYG-only active by purchasing credit before the 90-day expiry. Tello currently allows $10 SMS top-ups (ADD10PAYG) when a card is saved, while the website/manual PAYG purchase floor is $20. Because the SMS path itself depends on a working line, treat $40/year as the lowest documented maintenance path rather than a guaranteed universal checkout floor.

data.chinaActivation: Initial SIM/eSIM activation now explicitly requires physical presence in the United States and a first connection to Tello U.S. network towers. International roaming likewise requires prior U.S. line use. Do not present China-first activation as supported.
data.kyc: No ID verification; email + payment method only.
data.payment: International cards widely reported accepted; PayPal also accepted.
data.wifiCalling: Tello officially supports Wi-Fi Calling & Text abroad after U.S. activation, including OTP/verification SMS in its current help surfaces. 2026 community reports nevertheless show that overseas SMS can fail or stop on some lines, so treat it as useful but not guaranteed continuity.
data.roamingSms: International roaming in 200+ destinations draws from PAYG credit and requires prior U.S. line use. PAYG-only credit can fund roaming, but local partner availability and account/line state still matter.
data.holdReason: The route remains a valid real-mobile PAYG product, but it is not a safe China-first recommendation: first activation and roaming require prior U.S. network use, 2026 community reports include Codex verification-SMS failure and overseas SMS interruption, and account-security checks can disrupt continuity. Keep backstage and treat service-specific success as unquantified until exact PAYG-only app observations are independently reproduced.
data.tariffSummary: Initial/manual web PAYG purchase starts at $20. Standalone PAYG expires after 90 days; with a saved card, Tello documents $10 SMS top-ups (ADD10PAYG), yielding a lowest documented maintenance path of about $40 per 360 days. First activation and roaming require prior U.S. network use.
guideSteps: Buy at least $20 of PAYG credit and complete first activation while physically in the United States on Tello network towers.
For PAYG-only retention, renew before 90 days. A saved card enables documented $10 SMS top-ups; website/manual purchases still start at $20.
Before leaving the U.S., verify Wi-Fi Calling & Text and, if needed, enable international roaming after the line has been used on the U.S. network.
Treat overseas OTP/SMS as non-guaranteed: 2026 community evidence includes Codex verification failure and an abrupt overseas SMS interruption case.
Do not use this as a primary irreplaceable number without a recovery/port-out plan because account security checks are an unquantified continuity risk.
